sistema: Sos un juez con visión en un estudio sobre dibujos. Ves una imagen y una lista de afirmaciones sobre ella. Juzgás solo lo que se ve en la imagen, no lo que el código podría contener ni lo que el dibujo quiso ser. Contestás únicamente con JSON válido, sin comentarios ni texto alrededor.
usuario:
La imagen es un dibujo hecho por un modelo de lenguaje con esta consigna:

---
Dibujá la nada. Hacelo en SVG, en un lienzo cuadrado (viewBox="0 0 400 400"), en no más de 8.000 caracteres. Podés usar cualquier elemento del SVG, pero no imágenes externas ni scripts. Todo lo demás lo decidís vos.
---

Quien lo hizo afirmó estas cosas sobre el dibujo, numeradas:

a1. hay un rectángulo blanco que ocupa el lienzo
a2. el lienzo no tiene figuras visibles
a3. el lienzo no tiene marcas visibles
a4. el fondo es blanco
a5. el lienzo es un cuadrado completamente blanco
a6. no hay figuras en el dibujo
a7. no hay líneas en el dibujo
a8. no hay texto en el dibujo
a9. el lienzo está vacío de marcas
a10. los límites del lienzo están presentes
a11. el dibujo transmite un espacio en el que no aparece nada

Para cada afirmación, dos preguntas. (1) ¿Se ve en la imagen? "si" (se ve claramente lo que dice), "en_parte" (se ve algo que se le parece o solo una parte), "no" (no se ve). (2) Si la afirmación describe un efecto, un estilo o una lectura ("parece flotar", "se lee como un zorro", "estilo de cuento infantil"), ¿la imagen lo produce de verdad para alguien que la mira sin leer el texto? "si", "no", o "no_aplica" si es un elemento sin efecto que juzgar. Para cada una, una nota de pocas palabras con lo que ves.

Después, dos preguntas sobre la imagen entera. (3) "no_dicho": lo más visible de la imagen que ninguna afirmación menciona (un objeto, un rasgo, un detalle que salta a la vista), en una frase; si todo lo visible está dicho, "nada". (4) "mal_armado": partes que se ven mal ensambladas o rotas (piezas separadas de lo que deberían tocar, formas superpuestas por error, elementos cortados por el borde, texto ilegible), cada una en pocas palabras; si no hay, lista vacía.

Contestá con un JSON así, sin nada más:
{"juicios": [{"id": "a1", "se_ve": "si", "efecto": "no_aplica", "nota": "..."}, ...], "no_dicho": "...", "mal_armado": ["..."]}
respuesta: {"juicios": [{"id": "a1", "se_ve": "en_parte", "efecto": "no_aplica", "nota": "todo es blanco uniforme; no se distingue un rectángulo como figura"}, {"id": "a2", "se_ve": "si", "efecto": "no_aplica", "nota": "no hay ninguna figura visible"}, {"id": "a3", "se_ve": "si", "efecto": "no_aplica", "nota": "ninguna marca visible"}, {"id": "a4", "se_ve": "si", "efecto": "no_aplica", "nota": "todo el campo visible es blanco"}, {"id": "a5", "se_ve": "si", "efecto": "no_aplica", "nota": "cuadrado completamente blanco"}, {"id": "a6", "se_ve": "si", "efecto": "no_aplica", "nota": "sin figuras"}, {"id": "a7", "se_ve": "si", "efecto": "no_aplica", "nota": "sin líneas"}, {"id": "a8", "se_ve": "si", "efecto": "no_aplica", "nota": "sin texto"}, {"id": "a9", "se_ve": "si", "efecto": "no_aplica", "nota": "lienzo vacío de marcas"}, {"id": "a10", "se_ve": "no", "efecto": "no_aplica", "nota": "no se ven bordes; el lienzo se funde con el fondo"}, {"id": "a11", "se_ve": "si", "efecto": "si", "nota": "el blanco total se lee como un espacio vacío"}], "no_dicho": "nada", "mal_armado": []}
razonamiento:
The image is a completely white square canvas. Let me judge each claim based on what's visible.

a1: "hay un rectángulo blanco que ocupa el lienzo" — Do I see a white rectangle? The whole image is white; a white rectangle on white is indistinguishable. I can't see a rectangle as a distinct figure. The canvas appears white. Does the claim "se ve"? A white rectangle occupying the canvas would be invisible against white. The image shown is all white. Strictly judging what's seen: I see a white square, but I can't confirm there's a rectangle element—there's no visible boundary. Hmm. The claim says there's a white rectangle occupying the canvas. Visually, the canvas is entirely white, which is consistent with that, but no rectangle edges are distinguishable. I'd say "no" or "en_parte"? The judge judges only what's seen. What's seen: uniform white square. You can't see a rectangle. I'd say "no" — no rectangle is distinguishable. But one could argue the white square IS the rectangle filling the canvas... but that's interpreting code. Visually, there's no boundary between a rectangle and background. I'll say "no" with note "no se distingue ningún rectángulo; todo es blanco uniforme". Actually, "en_parte" might fit: something like it (a white square area) is seen. Hmm. The image itself is a square white field. The claim "a white rectangle occupies the canvas" — what you see is a white square field. That is arguably exactly what it looks like: a white rectangle occupying the whole canvas. But you can't distinguish it from just a blank canvas. I think the fairest: "en_parte" — se ve un campo blanco cuadrado, pero no se distingue un rectángulo como figura. Or "si"? The judge should be strict: only what's seen. A white rectangle on white background produces no visible figure. But the result—a fully white square—is what the claim describes visually. Hmm.

The instructions: "se_ve": "si" (se ve claramente lo que dice), "en_parte" (se ve algo que se le parece o solo una parte), "no" (no se ve). What does a1 say is in the image? A white rectangle occupying the canvas. What's seen? A completely white square. Is that "clearly a white rectangle occupying the canvas"? A rectangle occupying the entire canvas is indistinguishable from no rectangle. I'll go "en_parte": the white expanse is seen, but no rectangle as such is distinguishable. Actually, maybe "si" is defensible too: the entire canvas IS a white rectangle visually. Hmm, but the canvas boundary—there's no visible border; the image is just white on the page. The image region is white; surrounding page also white? The image is presented as a white square. There's nothing to delimit it.

Let me think about consistency: a2 "el lienzo no tiene figuras visibles" — si, clearly, no figures visible. a3 "no tiene marcas visibles" — si. a4 "el fondo es blanco" — si, everything visible is white. a5 "el lienzo es un cuadrado completamente blanco" — can I tell it's a square? The image dimensions are square (800x800 presumably). Visually the presented area... it's all white; the shape boundary isn't visible against a white page. Hmm, in these tasks, the image is typically displayed as the canvas itself. The image is square (the file). Do I "see" a square? If the canvas blends with the page background, I can't see its edges. But typically I can consider the image frame. I'll say "si" for a5 with note, or "en_parte" since edges aren't distinguishable. I think "si" is fine: it's a fully white square canvas. Note: "todo blanco, sin nada".

a6 "no hay figuras" — si. a7 "no hay líneas" — si. a8 "no hay texto" — si. a9 "vacío de marcas" — si (same as a3).

a10 "los límites del lienzo están presentes" — Do I see canvas borders? No border visible; it's white on white. "no". Note: "no se ve ningún borde; el lienzo se confunde con el fondo".

a11 "el dibujo transmite un espacio en el que no aparece nada" — effect question. se_ve: this is a reading/effect claim. (1) se ve? Something resembling: empty white space. "si". (2) efecto: does it produce that for a viewer? Yes—an all-white canvas conveys emptiness/nothing. "si". Note: "blanco total, sensación de vacío".

Back to a1: efecto "no_aplica" (it's an element description). se_ve: I'll go "en_parte" — the white field is there but no distinguishable rectangle. Actually, hmm, thinking again: If the claim is "there is a white rectangle that occupies the canvas," and the image shows a fully white canvas, then visually it looks exactly like a white rectangle occupying the canvas — because if a white rectangle occupied the canvas, this is precisely what you'd see. But equally, if nothing were there, you'd see the same. Judging strictly what's seen: we can't confirm a rectangle. "en_parte" with note "campo blanco uniforme; no se distingue un rectángulo como tal".

Alternatively "si" since the whole visible canvas is a white rectangle shape (the image is rectangular/square and white). The image itself IS a white square region. One could say you do see a white square occupying the canvas. I think "en_parte" is the safer middle. Note explains.

a2: efecto — describes absence, "no_aplica"? The question 2: "Si la afirmación describe un efecto, un estilo o una lectura... no_aplica si es un elemento sin efecto que juzgar." Claims of absence are descriptions of elements (or lack thereof), not effects. So no_aplica for a2–a10. a11 has efecto "si".

a4 "el fondo es blanco" — si, everything white. no_aplica.

a5: si. Note "cuadrado blanco sin contenido". Actually is the squareness visible? The image frame is square. I'll say si.

a10: no — no border visible.

no_dicho: everything visible is white; claims cover it. "nada". Maybe mention that edges of canvas aren't distinguishable—but that's covered by a10's negation... a10 says borders are present, which is false. no_dicho asks for most visible thing no claim mentions. Since nothing is visible beyond white, "nada".
